profile.name: Adam Grant
profile.headline: Organizational psychologist at Wharton, #1 NYT bestselling author of THINK AGAIN, host of the TED podcast Re:Thinking
profile.summary: Adam is an accomplished organizational psychologist, bestselling author, and professor based in Philadelphia. He has a deep passion for human behavior, writing, and intellectual discourse, frequently collaborating with notable thinkers and creators. Outside of his professional endeavors, he enjoys connecting with family and occasionally revisiting past athletic pursuits like diving.
needs: Intellectual stimulation and deep conversations
Mutual respect for independent careers
Shared commitment to personal growth
Playfulness and a sense of humor
Emotional intelligence and empathy
profile.communication_style: Thoughtful, articulate, and educational, balancing professional insights with accessible, engaging humor.
profile.lifestyle: Fast-paced and intellectually demanding, centered around academia, writing, media appearances, and public speaking, balanced with family time.
profile.looking_for: A curious, emotionally intelligent partner who values deep conversations, personal growth, and intellectual exploration.
evidence: Wharton professor and #1 NYT bestselling author of THINK AGAIN and HIDDEN POTENTIAL

profile.summary: Mel Robbins is a globally recognized podcaster, author, and entrepreneur dedicated to personal growth, mindset, and behavior change. Based in New England, she balances a high-profile media career with a grounded appreciation for family, seasonal changes, and home life. She brings immense energy, directness, and emotional intelligence to her professional and personal endeavors.
needs: Direct and honest communication without games
A partner who is securely confident and independent
Emotional depth and willingness to engage in personal growth
Appreciation for both high-achieving ambition and quiet domestic moments
Mutual respect for demanding professional schedules
values: Resilience in the face of change
profile.communication_style: Direct, articulate, encouraging, and radically honest
profile.lifestyle: Fast-paced media executive lifestyle balanced with quiet, nature-oriented country living in New England
dealbreakers: Inability to handle change or adversity
Negging or judgment of personal choices
profile.looking_for: An intellectually engaging, emotionally secure partner ready for a dynamic and supportive long-term partnership.
evidence: Host of award-winning The Mel Robbins Podcast and #1 NYT bestselling author of The Let Them Theory
Co-founder of Pure Genius Protein and CEO of 143 Studios
Graduated from Dartmouth College and Boston College Law School
Moved to Vermont and embraces New England seasonal changes like fall decorations and sunsets
Reflects publicly on turning 58 and starting over after a talk show cancellation and relocation
Shared personal milestones celebrating birthdays and family time on Instagram

By 33, I was Chief Revenue Officer at a venture-backed company, making more money than I’d ever imagined. And quietly falling apart.

I was burned out, anxious, drinking too much, and increasingly convinced that if I kept going, I might not see fifty.
Then one afternoon, in our house in Los Angeles, I had a panic attack so severe I ended up on the kitchen floor. 

My wife, Jennifer, called 911. The paramedics came. And by the time they were standing in our home, it was impossible to keep pretending this was just stress.

When it passed, I knew that the life I was building wasn’t the one I wanted to live.

So Jennifer and I quit our high-paying jobs with almost no plan. We bought a house in the mountains of Upstate New York, drove across the country, and started our lives over.

The real story is that I got my life back, slowly, unglamorously, one difficult choice at a time.

Today, I spend that life writing.

profile.summary: Justin is a seasoned entrepreneur and writer who previously suffered severe burnout in the corporate fast lane before completely restructuring his life for autonomy and balance. Today, he runs a successful one-person digital business from the US while sharing candid reflections on ambition, mental health, and lifestyle design. He values deep personal relationships, purposeful work, and protecting his time for family and downtime.
needs: A partner who values work-life balance and rejects toxic hustle culture
Mutual support for personal well-being, mental health, and stress management
Shared desire for autonomy, flexibility, and quality time together
Intellectual engagement and interesting conversations outside of routine work
profile.communication_style: Direct, thoughtful, vulnerable, and mentoring, often sharing personal lessons and clear insights.
profile.lifestyle: Location-independent or flexible, centered around low-overhead solo business operations, protecting weekends, prioritizing health, and maintaining an eclectic circle of friends.
dealbreakers: Workaholism that consumes personal life and relationships
Lack of ambition or personal accountability
profile.looking_for: A meaningful, balanced partnership with someone who enjoys life outside of work, values autonomy, and supports mutual growth.
evidence: By 33, I was Chief Revenue Officer at a venture-backed company... quietly falling apart.

So Jennifer and I quit our high-paying jobs with almost no plan. We bought a house in the mountains of Upstate New York...

Don't let work cause you to miss dinners, skip workouts, not see your family, or miss out on that vacation.
